So, let us remember some of the fun that was once had.

Error Messages

Putt's error messages always have a certain personality, whether it's with respect to replies to deleted comments, deleting deleted posts, or banning moderators. It's impossible to even scratch the surface of all the error messages to be found out there, but somehow all of them add something to the unique essence of Voat.

Error Pages

I'm not certain that Putt was alone in the involvement of the oldest and most well-known error page, but the newer iterations were likely entirely him. Putt has always been known for his descriptive messages.

Eastereggs

Both Atko and Putt have historically been involved in Voat eastereggs. Most of Atko's eastereggs were based in the Voat searchbar, which was removed quite some time ago. I recall reading that not all of his eastereggs were found -- and now I suppose they may never be. Putt, on the other hand, was responsible for all of the unique times-ago terms. I'm sure most users are well-acquainted with the terms "microcentury", "dog year", and "fortnight" -- and I'm sure there are some that remain undiscovered.

Trolling

Some users may remember when Voat had a totally serious change to a Drudge report-esque style, which happened to align with April first. The fact that it stuck around for a short time after April first was also totally normal. Putt (again, perhaps for this one also with Atko) also decided to troll those who attempted to simply erase their user bios. If you've ever erased your bio, give your profile a check -- perhaps it's not just empty space.

These examples again only scrape the surface of Putt's fun with Voat. An entire series of posts could be done on comments Putt has made over the years. The point is that for most of Voat's existence Putt had a very visible passion and love for the development of the platform, and that potential and character certainly remain. It is a great sadness if a recent burn-out (the cause of which may be tied in part to the issues I discuss in the >be PuttItOut post) will deprive both Voat and Putt of that fun-loving and passionate spirit forever, but I suspect that, eventually, things will return to how they were. Ebb and flow.
